senses.gloss:
kṛcchra
(‘that which produces suffering’)
------------------------------------------
When even extraordinary persons sometimes slip from the path of धर्म, no wonder then, that ordinary mortals are often tempted into committing sins and then get restless to get over the same. Prāyaścittas or expiations prescribed for the same include a general class known as कृच्छ्र. Another name for the same is प्राजापत्य.
Fasting (either partial or complete), bathing thrice a day, keeping vigil in the night, speaking the truth, offering तर्पण (oblations of water)—these are some of the disciplines included in it.
A very large number of kṛcchras have been mentioned in the works on the धर्मशास्त्रस् and पुराणस्, like कृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्र, gomūtrakṛcchra, jala or toya कृच्छ्र, तप्तकृच्छ्र and so on.

kṛcchrātikṛcchra
------------------------------------------
This is one of the varieties of कृच्छ्र, a penance to be performed for injuring others. The person who observes it has to subsist only on water for 21 or 24 days. If he is physically unable to do so, he should donate four milch cows.
See also KṚCCHRA.
